newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Disney set to show 2nd annual profit.
newsitem.headline: Euro Disney set to show 2nd annual profit.

text.p: Euro Disney is pulling out all the stops as it prepares to mark its fifth anniversary in 1997 -- a milestone many critics did not expect the theme park operator to celebrate.

Four years after a rocky start, Euro Disney is expected to confirm next month that its recovery is on track and its Disneyland Paris theme park a success by reporting a second consecutive annual profit.
Share analysts predict the company will report a net profit for the year ended on September 30 of between 160 million and 200 million francs ($31-39 million) on November 14 when its results are due.
Excluding exceptional items, analysts expect a 1995/96 profit ranging between 100 million and 140 million francs.

After losing more than seven billion francs in its first two years, Euro Disney emerged from the red for the first time last year when it reported a net profit of 114 million francs and a 21 percent jump in attendance to 10.7 million people.
Excluding an extraordinary gain from the repurchase of convertible bonds, its 1994/95 profit was two million francs.
Chairman Philippe Bourguignon said last month the company should "do better this year" after a "satisfying" summer season.
"The company is now at cruising speed and delivering operating cash flow, and the theme park is drawing crowds," a spokesman told Reuters last week.

Its performance has refuted doubters who said the Disney concept would flop in France, but the share is still worth only a fraction of its 1992 high above 160 francs. It was trading at 10.80 francs, up 0.25 franc, at midday on Tuesday.

Analyst Jacques Falzon at brokerage Transbourse expects Euro Disney to show a profit of 200 million francs -- on the high end of expectations -- but is wary of the stock. "It's very speculative. I don't recommend it based on the fundamentals."
Analysts say the theme park operator is weighed down by the costs of a 1994 six-billion-franc financial restructuring.
The deal pulled the company from the brink of failure and provided a brief debt holiday that allowed it to emerge from its losses, but the debt costs are being gradually phased in.

Although 1997 marks the fifth anniversary, which will be celebrated with customary Disney flare, including the unveiling of a new castle in January and a springtime festival, it will be a difficult year because of the rising charges.

Bourguignon last year said turnover would have to rise four to six percent a year to offset a rise in financial charges estimated at 100 million francs for the year just ended, 200 million for 1996/97, and another 100 million for 1997/98.
From 1998/99, royalties and management fees to 39-percent U.S. owner The Walt Disney Co will also be reinstated.
"They're having to run just to stand still," said analyst Nigel Reed at Paribas Capital Markets. "It's like being on a down escalator when you're trying to go up."
Analysts will be scrutinising attendance, hotel occupancy, and costs when the results are issued to gauge the company's prospects in a weak consumer spending climate in France.

Some suspect Euro Disney may have to seek a second debt restructuring, particularly if it has to sink money into its ambitious Phase II project which includes a 90,000 square metre shopping complex adjacent to the theme park in Marne-la-Vallee.
"They'll have to (restructure) because their debt is very heavy. But it's hard to know when," another analyst said.
"They need cash to pay down their debt, they need cash for new rides to refresh the park, and they also need cash if they're going to do Phase II," Reed said.
Euro Disney declined to comment on the restructuring talk.
The spokesman said the company would contribute "a very small fraction" of the five billion franc investment for the Phase II project, set to open in the year 2000.

Euro Disney plans to announce details of the retail and office developments at the end of November, after the deadline for appeals to the municipal clearance for the project. Local authorities gave their approval on September 30.
Euro Disney is also building a second convention centre and plans, further down the line, to build a second theme park.
